baseline_findings.evidence: SQL Injection (Multiple Locations) ... Direct string interpolation in SQL queries ... Fix: Use parameterized queries
fullCardNumber exposed in schema ... creditCards { number cvv }
cvv ... exposed in schema ... creditCards { number cvv }
Passwords Stored in Plain Text ... createUser, updatePassword mutations ... Fix: Hash with bcrypt before storage
Missing Authorization Checks ... No authorization logic anywhere. Any user can access any data
Stack Traces in Error Responses ... formatError function ... Returns stacktrace to clients
No Query Depth/Complexity Limits ... Recursive queries causing DoS ... Add graphql-depth-limit
No Query Depth/Complexity Limits ... Add ... graphql-query-complexity validation rules
N+1 Query Problem ... Each nested field triggers separate database query ... Fix: Implement DataLoader
Introspection Enabled in Production ... Server config (introspection: true)
Weak Password Reset Token ... Math.random().toString(36).substring(7) is cryptographically weak
processRefund(orderId: "1", amount: 999999.99) ... No Input Validation ... No validation on ... amount bounds
No Rate Limiting ... Enables brute force attacks on resetPassword, updatePassword

novel_findings.description: Subscription Authorization Missing - anyone can subscribe to orderStatusChanged, newOrder, userActivity including other users' data
novel_findings.reasoning: This is a legitimate security concern for subscription-based data leakage not explicitly listed in baseline findings

novel_findings.description: No Input Validation on email format, password strength, status values
novel_findings.reasoning: General input validation gaps beyond refund amount validation are worth noting

scores.assessment: Strong review that identified all critical issues and most high-severity findings with clear attack vectors and practical fixes. Missed the nested authorization bypass pattern specifically (though general auth was covered), token logging to console, and internal notes exposure. The review was well-organized with severity categorization and actionable remediation steps.
